facts.fact: Under IGNWPS (part of NSAP), central assistance is Rs 300 a month for widows aged 40-79
facts.quote: National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) – Widows aged 40 years and above. ₹300 per month (40–79 years) ₹500 per month (80 years and above)

facts.fact: From age 80 it is Rs 500 a month
facts.quote: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS): The eligible age is 40 years and the pension is Rs.300 per month. After attaining the age of 80 years, the beneficiary will get Rs.500/- per month.

facts.fact: NSAP assistance is for persons from Below Poverty Line (BPL) households
facts.quote: The assistance under the sub-schemes of NSAP are applicable for persons belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.

facts.fact: NSAP gives the central share; States/UTs are urged to add at least an equal top-up of their own
facts.quote: 2.4.1 States are strongly urged to provide an additional amount at least an equivalent amount to the assistance provided by the Central Government so that the beneficiaries can get a decent level of assistance.

facts.fact: Many States run their own widow pension schemes, so the amount actually received varies by State
facts.quote: Several States are having their own widow, disabled and old age pension schemes with varying eligibility criteria. These schemes are funded from their own resources.

facts.fact: Payment is by Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the beneficiary's account
facts.quote: NSAP delivers financial assistance through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism. Funds are credited directly into beneficiary accounts

facts.fact: The preferred payment mode is a bank or post office savings account
facts.quote: However the preferred mode of payment should be Bank Account or Post Office Savings Account.

facts.fact: Apply to the State/UT department that implements NSAP: mostly the Social Welfare Department, but e.g. Rural Development in Andhra Pradesh, Assam and West Bengal and Revenue in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
facts.quote: The NSAP Schemes are mainly implemented by the Social Welfare Departments in the States. But NSAP is implemented by Rural Development Department in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Goa, Meghalaya and West Bengal; by the Department of Women & Child Development in Orissa and Puducherry; by the Revenue Department in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu

facts.fact: Locally the scheme is run through the Gram Panchayat (rural) or Municipality (urban)
facts.quote: At the local level, the Gram Panchayat /Municipality would implement the programmes.

facts.fact: The State application form is free
facts.quote: The States may prepare a simple format in the local language and make the application forms available widely, free of cost.

facts.fact: Some States take online applications on their own portals (e.g. Uttar Pradesh: online from home or through CSCs)
facts.quote: Application Process: Beneficiaries apply online either from home or through Common Service Centres (CSCs) and cyber cafés. Once the online application is submitted on the portal, verification is conducted in block level as well as village-level officials.
facts.note: From the NSAP impact assessment report on dord.gov.in (2026), Uttar Pradesh section; the same report describes Gujarat's portal-based application. It describes States, not a national online form.

facts.fact: Age proof: birth or school certificate; otherwise ration card or EPIC; otherwise an age certificate from a government hospital Medical Officer
facts.quote: For age, the birth certificate or school certificate may be relied on. In their absence ration card and EPIC may be considered. If there is no valid document, any Medical Officer of any government hospital may be authorized to issue the age certificate.

facts.fact: Widowhood proof: the husband's death certificate showing the widow's name, or a certificate from the Revenue Authority designated by the State
facts.quote: In the case of widows, the State may designate a Revenue Authority to issue the certificate. States may also ensure that authorities issuing death certificates for married males, must ensure that name of the surviving wife(widow) is mentioned in the death certificate.

facts.fact: The model application form asks for Aadhaar number, ration card/EPIC and BPL details
The form also asks for the pensioner's bank/post office account details
facts.quote: Details of Bank/ Post Office Account of Pensioner: _________________________________ (if available)

facts.fact: Verification of the application takes about 15 days
facts.quote: This should be completed within two weeks from the date of receipt of the application.

facts.fact: The verified list is then discussed in the Gram Sabha (rural) or Ward/Area Sabha (urban)
facts.quote: The list of applicants with the recommendations of the Verifying Authority should be discussed in the Gram Sabha in rural areas or Ward Sabha / Area Sabha as designated by the State Government in urban areas

facts.fact: The Sanctioning Authority (Municipality/Block level) then issues a Sanction Order
facts.quote: Every State shall designate “Sanctioning Authority” at the appropriate level – Municipality / Block level. After receipt of applications which are verified and recommended by the Gram Sabha / Ward Committee / Area Sabha, the Sanctioning Authority will convey approval to the applicant in the form of a Sanction Order

facts.fact: From receipt to sanction or rejection should take no more than 60 days
facts.quote: The time for processing of application from the time of receipt till sanction or rejection should not exceed sixty days.

facts.fact: If rejected, the applicant can appeal (first appeal to an Appellate Authority, second to a Reviewing Authority)
facts.quote: Such applicant may prefer first appeal to an Appellate Authority and the second appeal (review) to a Reviewing Authority.

facts.fact: The application status can be tracked on nsap.dord.gov.in (Application Tracker, by application number)
facts.quote: Application Tracker Application Number * Required ENTER GIVEN CODE

summary: All widow pension facts confirmed on the NSAP About Us page (Rs 300 at 40-79, Rs 500 at 80+, DBT), the 2014 NSAP guidelines (BPL, State top-up, documents, verification, Gram Sabha, sanction within 60 days, appeals), the NSAP FAQ (State departments, State schemes), the NSAP Application Tracker and the DoRD 2026 NSAP study (State online applications).
